rv.q: A perceptive glimpse behind the curtain, I Hate Hamlet emerges as a touching, mirthful, and occasionally audacious love note to the people who create the magic of live theater.
So whether you loved or dreaded Shakespeare in high school or college, this may be the play for your next night out.
Ultimately, I Hate Hamlet lands as a production caught between charm and inconsistency.

cn.t: Critics find this revival of Rudnick's theatrical satire moderately entertaining, with strong performances and lively moments, though execution proves uneven. Shakespeare fans and theater insiders will likely enjoy it most.
